# Journal — S4a (site: success-cases, partners, marketplace, support)

- 14:48 Start. Read BRIEF.md, pages.json, looked at success-cases desktop ref tiles.
- 14:50 Setup: `npm create vite@latest . -- --template vue-ts`, installed the 3 tarballs + vue-router, ran `npx @aziontech/webkit init --yes`. init added eslint/stylelint/husky/tailwind v4 + postcss, `src/webkit.css`, `.claude/` bundle, AGENTS.md. Smooth (~5 min). **Works well.**
  - **low** — init pins 8 devDeps as `"latest"` and then `doctor` warns about its own choice ("consider pinning"). init should pin versions itself.
  - **low** — init adds `"prepare": "husky"` but the project has no git repo yet when you follow the README order (install → init). Had to `git init` before `npm install` to avoid husky complaining.
  - **medium** — Theme defaults to LIGHT; dark mode is `<html data-theme="dark">`. Only said in an init NOTE line; the site is dark-only, and nothing in the site sections/shell docs says how a dark-only site should force it. Used `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` in index.html.
- 14:50 Discovery: `llms/llms.txt` is the best map — the "Marketing sections" list has almost every band of these 4 pages (HeroBand, ClientMosaicColumns, StoryLibrary, RecognitionMarquee, ClosingCallToAction, HeroForm, StatsBand, CapabilityGrid, ClientQuotes, CompareSupportTiers, FaqSection, SiteNav, SiteFooter). ~15 min of reading. **Works well.**
  - **high** — Every marketing example uses asset URLs like `'/marketing-components/logos/magalu-extended-color.svg'` (client-mosaic-columns, story-library, recognition-marquee, client-quotes). These don't exist in a consumer app. Found the real form (`import x from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/<file>.svg'`) only by grepping package.json `exports` and reading quote-tabs' example. (The package's own docs/reviews/m2.7 FINDINGS lists the same issue as B1 — still unfixed in 5.12.0.)
  - **medium** — ClientMosaicColumns `brand: { base, glow }` and its example take hex colours (`#0e89ff`), which conflicts with the "tokens only / no hex" rule and the lint. Client brand colours have no tokens. Using theme primitives `var(--color-blue-500)` etc. as the closest.
- 14:56 **Page 1: site-success-cases — built.** HeroBand(centered-band) + ClientMosaicColumns + StoryLibrary + RecognitionMarquee + ClosingCallToAction(primary), SiteNav/SiteFooter in App.vue. First shot was already very close to the reference on desktop (height 5061 vs 5204). ~35 min incl. setup. **Works very well** — the section components map 1:1 to the reference bands.
  - **high** — `npm run build` (Vite template: `vue-tsc -b`) fails with TS2307 "Cannot find module '@aziontech/webkit/<name>'" for every subpath import, and TS2882 for `import '@aziontech/icons'` (the line init itself writes into main.ts). Oddly `vue-tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` resolves the same subpaths fine (verified it still catches real type errors). Fix: `declare module '@aziontech/icons'` in src/env.d.ts and build script = `vue-tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit && vue-tsc -p tsconfig.node.json --noEmit && vite build`. ~15 min. README claims vue-tsc works; it doesn't for the template's `-b` mode.
  - **medium** — the pre-commit hook init installs runs `npx eslint .` and `npx stylelint "**/*.{css,scss,vue}"` but init's eslint.config.mjs has no `ignores` and there is no .stylelintignore, so after the first `npm run build` the hook lints `dist/` (575 errors from WebKit's own compiled CSS/JS: hex colours, literal ms) and blocks every commit. Added `{ ignores: ['dist/**'] }` and a .stylelintignore. ~5 min.
  - **low** — the lint bans all comments in app code (`webkit/authoring-standards`), including the comment create-vite puts in vite.config.ts. Surprising for a consumer app; removed them.
  - **low** — SiteNav shows the Login button on iPhone; the reference hides it below xl (only hamburger, wordmark, Start for free, search). No prop to control it.
  - **low** — SiteFooter links have no "external" flag, so "Our Community ↗" loses its external icon.
  - **low** — StoryLibrary card description renders smaller and muted; the reference shows it larger in white. No prop; left as is (no restyling).
  - **low** — ClientMosaicColumns: the reference faces are flat colour; WebKit draws a glow gradient. Fine.
  - Note: theme font is Rubik while the reference uses Sora-like face; the package's own docs/reviews/m2.9-site-parity.md says that is a deliberate theme decision. Not fixable without restyling.
- 14:57 **Page 2: site-partners — built.** HeroForm (fields as data, local validation, submit → mock loading/submitted) + StatsBand + SectionModule(kind=left) wrapping a bare CapabilityGrid with `pi pi-check` glyphs. Desktop height 2532 vs ref 2531; iPhone 2807 vs 2788. ~20 min. **Works very well** — HeroForm reproduces the whole form (Required tags, half-width pairs, +1 phone, selects, orange submit) from data.
  - **medium** — HeroForm's field type: passing a plain array of objects fails vue-tsc (`kind: string` not assignable to `HeroFormFieldKind`). The docs never say the types are importable; found by reading hero-form.vue that `import type { HeroFormField } from '@aziontech/webkit/hero-form'` works. The JSON API / llms page should list the exported types. ~5 min.
  - **medium** — CapabilityGrid's `title` is always centered; the reference "Why you should be a partner…" header is left-aligned. No `kind`/alignment prop. Used SectionModule(kind=left, title) + bare CapabilityGrid instead — visually right, but then CapabilityGrid renders each item heading as h2 (reference: h3) because it only drops to h3 when it owns the title. Semantic gap.
  - **low** — HeroForm title doesn't break into "Grow as an / Azion Partner" like the reference (WebKit keeps it on one line at a smaller size). No title-length prop on HeroForm (HeroBand has `titleLength`).
  - **low** — StatsBand: `value: '3k'` renders "3K" (uppercased by the mono face) — matches the reference anyway.
- 14:59 **Page 3: site-marketplace — built.** HeroBand(kind=centered, dot field, client ticker via `carouselMarks` registry names) + SectionModule > CardGrid(kind=frame, flush) > CardGridCell > Topic (heading-level 3, `href` on "Licensing Flexibility" gives the ↗ link cue) + SectionModule(eyebrow/title/description, kind=left) > CapabilityGrid + ClientQuotes. Desktop 3407 vs 3468; iPhone 3348 vs 3418. ~25 min. **Works well.**
  - **medium** — No section for "a bare row of three claims where one is a link, no icons, no title". CapabilityGrid has no per-item `href`, ContentColumns has none either, UseCaseLinks makes every item a link and needs an icon. Composed CardGrid(frame)+CardGridCell+Topic, which worked first time; the `Topic.href` trailing arrow is exactly the reference's ↗. The card-grid llms page lists `CardGrid.Cell` but the import `@aziontech/webkit/card-grid-cell` is only visible in one example.
  - **medium** — HeroBand `headerOffset` wants "the height of the site header" but there is no token for it (SiteNav is `h-14` inside GlobalHeader). Used `calc(var(--spacing) * 14)` after reading global-header.vue. A `--site-header-height` token (or SiteNav exposing it) would remove the guesswork.
  - **medium** — ClientQuotes/QuoteTabs need a quote per client card. pages.json only gives the Contabilizei quote; the reference wall shows 6 clients (Contabilizei, Axur, Zoop, HeroSpark, GPA, GFG). Used WebKit's own example quotes for Axur/Zoop/HeroSpark and short mock lines for GPA and GFG (mock data, not visible until the carousel advances).
  - **low** — HeroBand on iPhone: the reference title wraps to 3 lines at a larger size; `titleLength="long"` keeps 2 lines at a smaller size. Left as is.
  - **low** — the card-grid example imports `CardGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/card-grid'` + `CardGridCell from '@aziontech/webkit/card-grid-cell'`; copying that verbatim fails lint `webkit/prefer-tree-shakeable-root` (wants `card-grid-root`). Example and lint disagree.
- 15:01 **Page 4: site-support — built.** HeroBand(centered-band, large, client ticker) + bare CapabilityGrid (3 pillars, h2 like the reference) + CompareSupportTiers (2 bands, 4 tiers, Enterprise highlighted, picker fold on iPhone) + ClientQuotes + FaqSection (11 questions) + ClosingCallToAction(split). Desktop 5681 vs 5724; iPhone 5335 vs 5593. ~30 min. **Works very well** — CompareSupportTiers reproduces the whole table, sticky header, accent bar and mobile tier picker from data.
  - **high** — `compare-support-tiers.vue` itself fails vue-tsc: 6× TS2304 "Cannot find name 'section'/'sectionIndex'" (template v-for scope inside WebKit's SFC). Because WebKit ships .vue source, a consumer's type-check inherits it and `npm run build` fails; skipLibCheck can't help. (Same class of bug the package's own m2.7 FINDINGS X1 records for compare-plans.vue.) Workaround: tsconfig `paths` maps `@aziontech/webkit/compare-support-tiers` to a local `DefineComponent` d.ts shim, so only that one import loses prop types. ~10 min.
  - **medium** — HeroBand kinds are hard to tell apart from the docs: `centered` "fills a screen" vs `centered-band` "large site-wide band". First tried `centered plain` + headerOffset; the hero was a full screen tall on iPhone. `centered-band size=large` matched the reference pixel-for-pixel on both widths. A picture per kind (or "use X for listing/hub pages") would save the trial and error. ~10 min.
  - **medium** — FaqSection needs an answer per question; pages.json gives only the 11 questions (answers are collapsed in the reference). Wrote short mock answers consistent with the tier table.
  - **low** — ClientQuotes doesn't expose QuoteTabs' `autoplay`, so the band moves on to the 2nd client (Axur) during a 2.5 s screenshot, while the reference shows Contabilizei. Can't pin it without going below the section.
  - **low** — CompareSupportTiers requires `description` per tier ("who it is for"), but the reference header shows only name + button; passed empty strings (nothing rendered, good).
- 15:03 Final pass: `npm run build` passes (vue-tsc app + node, vite build, dist/404.html copy); `npx @aziontech/webkit check` → 0 errors, 1 warning (the init-made "latest" pins); `vite preview` serves /, all 4 routes and an unknown deep path with index.html. Shot all 4 pages at the end (no page errors). Dev server stopped.
- Summary of what worked well: llms.txt as a map; the marketing *sections* (one prop object per band, almost no composition needed); HeroForm/CompareSupportTiers/StoryLibrary as data-driven bands with real behaviour (validation, filters, tier picker); SectionContainer/SectionGap keep the side rules continuous for free; SiteNav/SiteFooter reproduce the chrome incl. mobile drawer. Total ≈ 2 h 45 min, of which ~45 min was friction (typecheck, lint hook, asset URLs, picking hero kinds).

# DONE — job S4a (site)

## Pages
- `site-success-cases`: **built** — hero, 3 coloured featured tiles, filterable story library (search + 3 facets + Load more), analyst marquee, closing CTA. Gaps: brand faces use theme primitives (no client-colour tokens); story text smaller/muted than the reference; theme font differs (Rubik vs reference face).
- `site-partners`: **built** — form hero (all 9 fields, Required tags, +1 phone, selects, mock submit), stats band, "Why…" grid. Gap: grid item headings are h2 (reference h3) because the left-aligned title had to come from SectionModule.
- `site-marketplace`: **built** — dot-field hero with client ticker, 3 value cells (one linked), "What is the Azion Marketplace?" + 3 checks, client quotes wall. Gap: quotes for clients other than Contabilizei are mock/WebKit-example text (not in pages.json).
- `site-support`: **built** — hero with ticker, 3 pillars, full tier comparison table (2 bands, 4 tiers, Enterprise highlighted, mobile tier picker), client quotes, FAQ (11 questions), split closing CTA. Gap: FAQ answers are mock (only questions given); quotes band autoplays past Contabilizei.

## WebKit pieces used most
SectionContainer + SectionGap (every page), SiteNav, SiteFooter, HeroBand (centered-band / centered), CapabilityGrid, SectionModule, ClientQuotes, HeroForm, StatsBand, StoryLibrary, ClientMosaicColumns, RecognitionMarquee, CompareSupportTiers, FaqSection, ClosingCallToAction, CardGrid + CardGridCell + Topic, WebkitProvider, `@aziontech/webkit/assets/*` logos, `carouselMarks` registry names.

## Top 5 problems with WebKit (by impact)
1. **Build breaks on WebKit's own code / typing** — the Vite template's `vue-tsc -b` can't resolve `@aziontech/webkit/<name>` subpaths, `import '@aziontech/icons'` (written by init) has no types, and `compare-support-tiers.vue` itself fails vue-tsc (TS2304 `section`). Needed a custom build script, an env.d.ts declaration and a `paths` shim. (high)
2. **Examples use asset URLs that don't exist in a consumer app** (`/marketing-components/logos/…`); the working `@aziontech/webkit/assets/<file>` import form is only discoverable from package.json exports. (high)
3. **init's pre-commit hook blocks every commit after the first build** — eslint/stylelint configs don't ignore `dist/`, so WebKit's own compiled CSS/JS fails the lint. (medium)
4. **Layout gaps in sections without escape hatches** — CapabilityGrid title can't be left-aligned (forces a SectionModule wrapper and wrong heading levels), no linked item in CapabilityGrid/ContentColumns, ClientQuotes hides `autoplay`, SiteNav always shows Login on mobile, SiteFooter has no external-link flag, no site-header-height token for `headerOffset`. (medium)
5. **Docs ambiguity that costs trial and error** — HeroBand `centered` vs `centered-band` vs `title-band` only distinguishable by trying; exported prop types (`HeroFormField`) undocumented; card-grid example imports contradict the lint (`prefer-tree-shakeable-root`); hex colours in ClientMosaicColumns examples vs the "tokens only" rule; dark-only site setup only mentioned in an init NOTE. (medium)

## Build
`npm run build` **passes** (vue-tsc app + node, `vite build`, `dist/404.html` fallback copy). `dist/` serves as a static SPA (verified with `vite preview`: `/`, all four routes and an unknown deep path return index.html). `npx @aziontech/webkit check`: 0 errors, 1 warning. Git: 4 commits in `app/` (setup+page 1, then one per page).
